**Finding: compliant** — no redline proposed.

The ownership package (§§14.1–14.4, supported by §13.2 and §15.1) satisfies our preferred position:

- **Customer Data / Customer IP (§14.1):** we own it; Vendor gets only a limited processing right to deliver the Services. No assignment to Vendor.
- **Deliverables (§14.2):** vest in us on creation (subject to payment of Fees), with an express Vendor assignment of worldwide right, title and interest, personnel assignments, and further assurances.
- **Vendor IP (§14.3 + §13.2):** Vendor retains Vendor Technology (acceptable), but embedded Vendor Technology carries a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence to use, modify and create derivative works, extending to Affiliates and contractor support. Vendor must also flag material Vendor Technology pre-delivery and cannot embed restrictive third-party material without our approval.
- **No joint ownership (§14.4):** expressly excluded absent a signed instrument; feedback use is limited to generalized, de-identified suggestions and we keep unrestricted rights in our own feedback.
- **§15.1** adds protection against sale, advertising use, commingling and model training on Customer Data.

Noted in the rationale but not flagged: Deliverable ownership is conditioned on payment of Fees, and the §13.2 sublicensing right is framed as permitting contractors to support the material rather than a general sublicence right — both minor sub-elements short of ideal wording, not material deviations.
